newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's NSW state asks for tax compensation.
newsitem.headline: Australia's NSW state asks for tax compensation.

text.p: Australia's most populous state, New South Wales, said on Tuesday it would ask the national government to top up its revenue after a landmark court ruling outlawing lucrative state fees on alchohol, tobacco and petrol.
State premier Bob Carr told reporters the High Court ruling would cost his state A$1.8 billion a year.

"These taxes are now rendered illegal and invalid," Carr said. "It's important we negotiate with the Commonwealth (federal) government compensation so the states can continue to run the frontline services the states have to manage."

In a four to three majority ruling earlier on Tuesday, the High Court of Australia ruled that state business franchise fees were in fact an excise, which only the national government can raise under Australia's constitution.
"We are conscious that this judgment has the most serious implications for the revenues of the states and territories," said the four majority judges, including chief judge Gerard Brennan.

Constitutional experts said the Federal government would have to swiftly levy its own taxes to replace the state charges, which account for about 16 percent of the income raised by Australia's six states and two territories.
Carr, labelling the judgment a constitutional crisis, also urged the Federal government to legislate to prevent retailers and wholesalers reclaiming the state levies already paid.
The states and territories already rely on Canberra for about half their income, divided up at a traditionally annual acrimonious summit of state, territory and national leaders.
